text.p: The following are the main stories from Thursday morning's German newspapers:
FRANKFURTER ALLGEMEINE ZEITUNG
- Health Minister Horst Seehofer calls for a more comprehensive cattle slaughter to wipe out mad cow disease.
- Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel calls for "fair treatment" of Turkey.
- Officials agree on solution to problem of paying back money borrowed by local councils from East German government.
- Association of German Employers (BDA) rejects pension reform plans.
- IG Metall trade union vows to fight government tax reform proposals.
HANDELSBLATT
- German car industry reclaims leading position in world markets thanks to new models and advantageous exchange rates.
- Confederation of German Industry (BDI) supports government tax reform plan.
- Government and regional states agree changes to working conditions for public servants.
- Constructors' trade association calls for privately financde motorway construction.
SUEDDEUTSCHE ZEITUNG
- Chancellor Helmut Kohl faces massive criticism from party leadership over his handling of recent debates over pensions and tax reform.
- Leader of textiles trade union calls for Kohl to resign.
- Paul Friedhoff becomes economics spokesman for centrist Free Democrats (FDP).
- Kohl praises Ludwig Erhard, father of West Germany's post-war "economic miracle".
- Mechanical engineering sector hopes for revival in fortunes in 1997.
DIE WELT
- FDP plans to present its own plans for reforming pensions system.
- Germans lead the world in travelling and tourism, statistics show.
- Germany faces fine from Brussels for not applying European Union environmental guidelines.
